newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Amvesco targets 35 pct op margin.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Amvesco targets 35 pct op margin.

text.p: Fund management group Amvesco plc is aiming for a 35 percent operating margin in 1997, following its merger with AIM Management Group Inc, Robert McCullough, chief financial officer, told Reuters.

The group on Thursday announced a 23.6 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profits, driven by contributions across the board. It said the U.S. institutional business benefited from rising equity markets, with the international unit profiting from prior years' investment strategy.
Pre-tax profits of 66 million sterling in 1996 did not include results for AIM, where McCullough said net income rose 85 percent in the year to $89 million. The merger was completed on February 28.
Amvesco's operating margin was 27.2 percent in 1996.
In its results, it said European and Pacific regions had been combined into a new global business unit headed by management team member Michael Benson.
The unit is also responsible for South America and the North American marketing of global products.
McCullough said funds under management at the combined operation were $165.2 billion at end-February 1997.

At Amvesco, funds under management were up 13 percent at $94.5 billion at end-1996 despite a net loss of funds under management in its U.S. institutional business due to investors' movement to higher yielding investments from fixed income securities, where over one-third of assets are placed.
But the institutional business had a record year in attracting new business, and the individual services group saw net assets under management grow $4.9 billion.
The European retail business saw its highest levels of new business for some years, and Asian operations had picked up some high quality institutional mandates.

McCullough said the group was always on the lookout for expansion opportunities, and would consider either acquisitions or starting up operations, specifically in the Pacific region, with Latin America also offering good potential.
"We continue to look to expand our opportunities in the Pacific Basin. Australia is the obvious target there and we have looked at that and Singapore," he said.
The group expected to set up a physical presence in Germany this year after adding Italy and the Netherlands in 1996.
He said a correction in US equities was likely, although it was impossible to predict the timing.
"We would be naive to say that there won't be a correction," he said. Group budgeting assumes no change.
He also said Amvesco, having changed its name from Invesco due to the merger with AIM, would have to change its name again following a legal challenge from a company of the same name.
The name would be changed to Amvescap Plc, subject to shareholder approval at a May 8 meeting.
